answer_1.quote: LLMs frequently produce unnatural texts resembling translationese in monolingual natural language generation tasks
answer_1.outputs: translations from English to Chinese, German, and French

answer_2.quote: We compare T-index with several supervised and unsupervised baselines on synthetic and human-annotated data

answer_3.quote: We further include LLM-as-a-judge method for comparison: LLama3.3-Instruct-70B and Qwen2.5-Instruct-72B

answer_4.quote: each annotator is presented with a source text and a translation. The annotator is asked to rate the translation on a 6-point Likert scale ranging from 0-5, where a higher rating indicates more translationese. ... the annotator is presented with a pair of translations, with the source text, and forced (without a tie) to choose the one that exhibits more translationese
answer_4.guideline: Pointwise: rate translationese degree on 0-5 scale; Pairwise: select translation with more translationese given source text
